a.title: Parallel contrast mode
a.mechanism: Offer ordinary/parallel estimate presentations only where duration is meaningful; keep explicit state and stable scoped routes.
a.visible: Applicable estimate view, exact period, active scope, title and completion.
a.disclosed: Both views retain per-task Details, section options/inclusion and header diagnostics/breakdowns; no duration setting changes merely from switching views.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
a.benefit: Lets complex concurrency be inspected without making every list equally dense.
a.risk: An extra presentation selector adds one control.
a.verification: Switch views with open disclosures, complete a task, edit duration and verify all totals/data remain identical.

b.title: Ledger with single material toolbar
b.mechanism: Retain the flat ledger and single glass toolbar; use labelled aligned totals where space permits, replace narrow supplemental task fields with an expandable detail line, and preserve exact period, scope, all original field actions and menus.
b.visible: Dates, count, duration and price in labeled aligned ledger fields. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
b.disclosed: Field buttons reveal original editors and source breakdowns; scope selector, routine diagnostic and full menus remain in toolbar/section controls; supplemental metadata expands beneath task. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
b.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
b.benefit: Keeps substantial information visible without visual surface inflation.
b.risk: Many fields may require responsive column priorities.
b.verification: Check 320px field stacking, shopping exceptions, parallel versus active totals and focus targets.

a.title: Depth-independent context rows
a.mechanism: Keep small hierarchy guides; place period/scope and Details outside indentation with full ancestor descriptions.
a.visible: Hierarchy cue, full-width context, counts, title and completion.
a.disclosed: Context row exposes period, duration and inclusion; Options opens existing section menu; task Details retains every editor and navigation link. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
a.benefit: Metadata remains readable even at deep nesting.
a.risk: Reduced indentation can weaken parent-child recognition.
a.verification: Verify five-level nesting, screen-reader path, drag affordances, mixed periods and mobile widths.

b.title: Focusable side inspector
b.mechanism: Keep the focusable side inspector when content width permits and use its sheet otherwise; preserve exact subject, period and inclusion labels, return focus to the opener or safe fallback after deletion, and keep all original object actions.
b.visible: Identity, period, scope summary and completion. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
b.disclosed: Inspector shows all object-specific facts and existing actions, including diagnostic, estimates, section menus and metadata editor shortcuts. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
b.access: 44px inspectors; labelled panel, explicit close, predictable focus return; no focus-triggered automatic opening. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
b.benefit: Avoids shifting the list whenever a keyboard user inspects properties.
b.risk: Desktop panel reduces available task width.
b.verification: Test selected object changes, deleted task focus fallback, mobile sheet trapping and every metadata action.

a.title: Period watermark heading
a.mechanism: Keep the exact period heading and Periodo button; repeat local exceptions and reference dates in completion descriptions.
a.visible: Exact period, list identity, active scope, completion and divergent section context.
a.disclosed: A Periodo button reveals the existing navigator; summary retains status/estimates; task details retains all properties and section menus remain visible.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
a.benefit: Makes temporal orientation stronger than ornamental badges.
a.risk: Persistent date text consumes header height.
a.verification: Navigate to past weeks/months and confirm status, section context and task completion all use the same reference date.

b.title: Three disclosure shelves
b.mechanism: Use independent Resumen, Alcance and Propiedades shelves; keep scope and local override words beside closed summaries.
b.visible: Exact period, active inclusion, local overrides, plain titles, completion and shelf controls.
b.disclosed: Page shelf exposes diagnostic and duration routes; section shelf exposes inclusion and breakdown; task shelf contains all metadata actions and links.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
b.benefit: Keeps object scope local and makes hidden information predictable.
b.risk: Expanded shelves can lengthen the virtualized list.
b.verification: Measure shelf-height integration, 320px wrapping, inclusion toggles and completion without accidental shelf activation.

a.title: Frequency map disclosure
a.mechanism: Provide one Frequency map with labeled page and section groups; bound its height and retain local path context.
a.visible: Exact period, active scope, counts, completion and recurrence exceptions.
a.disclosed: Map provides page/section composition and inclusion control; task Details retains original frequency picker and every metadata action; diagnostic and menus remain dedicated.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
a.benefit: One map gives composition a meaningful home.
a.risk: Map can become too large for small mobile screens.
a.verification: Check daily/weekly/monthly/yearly contributions, collapsed sections and map focus restoration.

b.title: Inherited context line
b.mechanism: Print labeled view context per matching block; show differing deadlines/scope and describe inherited context accessibly.
b.visible: Exact period, scope phrase, counts, completion and differing deadlines.
b.disclosed: Context button exposes period navigation, include controls and duration; task Details always expose complete original metadata; Options retain all menus. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
b.benefit: Removes repeated information while making the source legible.
b.risk: Inherited context could be mistaken for a task's own setting.
b.verification: Verify differing frequencies, historical dates, same-period tasks, metadata editors and narrow wrapping.

a.title: Caregiver scope confirmation sentence
a.mechanism: Write one global period/inclusion sentence; use short local captions and explicit differing overrides.
a.visible: Exact period, included/not-included words, title/check and specific due context.
a.disclosed: A Cambiar alcance control opens existing scope choices plus counts; Resumen contains estimates/status; Detalles and scoped menus retain all actions.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
a.benefit: Makes the boundary of today's visible work explicit for interrupted reading.
a.risk: Repeated scope sentences can still feel dense.
a.verification: Compare page/section overrides, full versus own totals, historical references and task date/frequency/duration actions at 375px.

b.title: Period provenance captions
b.mechanism: Use one provenance caption per matching block; show local scope or recurrence exceptions with direct context disclosure.
b.visible: Period, active scope, counts, completion and differing frequency/date context.
b.disclosed: Provenance button opens navigator, scope settings and diagnostic; task Details exposes full metadata including hidden matches; Options remains available. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
b.benefit: Shows where accumulated maintenance work comes from.
b.risk: Repeated provenance captions can be lengthy.
b.verification: Verify own/accumulated totals, mixed-frequency sections, custom cycles, reference dates and mobile wrapping.

a.title: Completion lane
a.mechanism: Retain leading completion and trailing inspection lanes; bound desktop row width, use object-specific inspection labels, and keep period, included scope and original Start eligibility visible.
a.visible: Leading completion targets, titles, selected week, included-scope phrase and Start. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
a.disclosed: Trailing Details opens task metadata; Inspection opens existing duration diagnostics and inclusion controls; Options exposes unchanged menus. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping lanes, descriptive completion names and keyboard order. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
a.benefit: Reduces accidental editing while marking many household tasks complete.
a.risk: Trailing controls may be distant on wide screens.
a.verification: Test partial repetitions, blocked tasks, accidental propagation, scope toggles and narrow lanes.

b.title: Section action shelf
b.mechanism: Keep section commands in one local shelf with independent collapse and persistent inclusion captions.
b.visible: Global period/scope, section title/count/inclusion, collapse, Actions, title and due exceptions.
b.disclosed: Shelf contains existing section menu route, include-frequency control, duration breakdown and start callback; global options and task metadata remain available. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
b.benefit: Scope of every action becomes spatially explicit.
b.risk: Open shelves can make long lists taller.
b.verification: Check sibling actions never affect another section, drag behavior, accumulated scope and keyboard collapse.

a.title: Single task action lane
a.mechanism: Retain separate completion and information lanes, stack the trailing lane for narrow nested rows, and keep due exceptions plus period/scope visible while information exposes every original editor and link.
a.visible: Completion, title, due exception, period and separate scope text. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
a.disclosed: Information opens metadata editor routes; page summary opens durations/status; section options retains inclusion and configuration. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
a.access: Nonoverlapping 44px lanes; keyboard order completion then information; reduced-motion scoped feedback. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
a.benefit: Separates completing from inspecting so dense metadata cannot steal a tap.
a.risk: Information buttons repeat on every task.
a.verification: Verify rapid adjacent completion taps, nested subtasks, list navigation links and no propagation into row actions.

b.title: Measured wrapping priority
b.mechanism: Wrap by available content width with stable trigger nodes; avoid replacing focused controls or open-panel launchers.
b.visible: Title/check, exact period, active scope, counts and deadline exceptions.
b.disclosed: Details retains full metadata action rows; header/section summary reveals estimates and breakdown; all options, diagnostics, inclusion and navigational links stay reachable.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
b.benefit: Responsive layout follows content pressure without trimming essential context.
b.risk: Threshold changes can cause distracting layout shifts.
b.verification: Resize with open menus and keyboard focus; test 320px/375px, long labels, reduced motion and selector preservation.

a.title: Single-column command stack
a.mechanism: Use one-column title/context/command order; collapse metadata initially and retain an obvious scoped close control.
a.visible: Title/check, exact period, active scope, section count and named commands.
a.disclosed: Details unfolds metadata as full-width 44px action rows; summary/diagnostic, inclusion and original page/section options use the same stack, retaining rich links.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
a.benefit: No horizontal competition or tiny tappable metadata.
a.risk: Vertical height increases in expanded states.
a.verification: Inspect 320px/375px long Spanish labels, zoom, options reachability and completion targets.

b.title: Named summary drawer
b.mechanism: Keep the named summary drawer; label page and section summaries by object, keep exact period and scope beside the opener, and expose a compact estimate preview only when relevant.
b.visible: Title, selected period, task completion and explicit Resumen/Detalles labels. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
b.disclosed: A summary drawer groups accumulated scope, estimates and diagnostics; task details retain each metadata edit; existing list and section menus stay separately named. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
b.access: Native 44px buttons, labelled dialog, focus return and visible focus. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
b.benefit: Makes the next action obvious without requiring icon literacy.
b.risk: A drawer may add a step to planning.
b.verification: Complete a task; open scope and duration breakdown; change a historical period and edit every metadata field at 320px.

a.title: Context-first mobile folio
a.mechanism: Place wrapping context before titles in one column; repeat section captions only when context differs.
a.visible: Exact period, inclusion wording, title/check, counts and due exceptions.
a.disclosed: A full-width Details row opens existing metadata actions and breakdowns; Options and routine inclusion use separate controls rather than competing trailing icons; estimates/diagnostic remain obvious.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
a.benefit: Readable context establishes meaning before dense titles.
a.risk: More lines may delay the first task on initial load.
a.verification: Test long list/section/task titles, historical dates, rollover and scrolling without stale captions.

b.title: Deadline exceptions shelf
b.mechanism: Suppress only safely redundant dates; always retain overdue and divergent deadlines against the selected reference date.
b.visible: Exact shared period, active scope, exception deadlines, titles and completion.
b.disclosed: A Dates disclosure lists every omitted date and original date editor; task Details keeps remaining metadata; estimate, diagnostic, inclusion and options controls remain discoverable.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
b.benefit: Eliminates repeated date badges while retaining urgent exceptions.
b.risk: Incorrect equivalence rules could conceal a meaningful date.
b.verification: Verify reference-date comparisons, weekly/monthly contexts and date restoration in disclosures.

a.title: Return-to-work checkpoint
a.mechanism: Keep the return-to-work checkpoint beside original Start, showing exact selected period and own/accumulated scope; repeat local checkpoints only for actual differences and preserve original eligibility, diagnostics, estimates and all editing routes.
a.visible: Checkpoint, title, counts, scope and task completion. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
a.disclosed: Checkpoint opens existing navigator, diagnostics, accumulated setting and estimates; Start calls original callback; Details and Options preserve all remaining actions. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
a.access: 44px controls, explicit date labels, focus management and unchanged completion semantics. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
a.benefit: Returning users can understand what they are about to act on.
a.risk: Extra checkpoint may feel repetitive across sections.
a.verification: Verify missed periods, partial targets, selected dates, scope callback independence and 320px.

b.title: Stable focus emphasis
b.mechanism: Keep labeled controls fixed with adequate resting contrast; emphasize only the focused containing row without revealing new commands.
b.visible: Completion, title, exact period, active scope and visible Details/Options.
b.disclosed: Expanded summaries expose dense facts; focused row gains contrast and descriptive hint while metadata actions remain accessible through details.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
b.benefit: Helps users locate keyboard position in a restrained visual hierarchy.
b.risk: Overemphasis could turn every tab stop into visual noise.
b.verification: Tab through nested tasks and menus; compare unfocused/focused screenshots and ensure controls remain visible on touch.

a.title: Context before options
a.mechanism: Keep Context as a read-only first surface, show exact period and own/accumulated scope before opening, and put original scope, estimate and period controls directly beside their summary values.
a.visible: Title, selected period, scope summary, completion and Context. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
a.disclosed: Summary provides full data and routes to unchanged navigator, toggles, menus and focused task editors; no summary click directly mutates. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
a.access: 44px links, accessible dialog heading and reliable focus return. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
a.benefit: Inspection is safe while remembering the app after absence.
a.risk: Extra routing increases taps to management commands.
a.verification: Verify every preserved command route, changing context freshness, historical dates and mobile sheet.

b.title: Semantic one-line status replacement
b.mechanism: Replace progress duplicates with one count-first sentence distinguishing own completion and included pending work.
b.visible: Selected period, inclusion state, count sentence, completion and relevant due context.
b.disclosed: Status sentence opens existing diagnostic; secondary disclosures retain duration, scope and task editing; options remain separately scoped.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
b.benefit: Removes redundant progress signals while keeping spoken information complete.
b.risk: A sentence may wrap differently as counts change.
b.verification: Test all_done, own-done/accumulated-pending, zero-goal and historical states; confirm diagnostic selectors and duration routes survive.

a.title: Outline with inline inspector
a.mechanism: Use an outline with local inline inspectors before section tasks; keep collapse independent and avoid duplicate menu routes.
a.visible: Headings/counts, exact period, active scope, title/check and Details.
a.disclosed: Inline inspector includes estimates, accumulated control and section Options; task details contains all original metadata actions; global menu remains visible. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
a.benefit: Supporting information stays beside the correct hierarchy node.
a.risk: Many open inspectors could become visually dense.
a.verification: Verify collapse/disclosure independence, virtualized sizes, all actions, referenceDate and 320px.

b.title: Duration emphasis without movement
b.mechanism: Use tabular duration tiers without rearranging tasks; retain equally legible urgency and omit inapplicable duration.
b.visible: Estimates, title/check, exact dates and explicit accumulated scope.
b.disclosed: Each estimate opens DurationInfoCard; task Details retains full metadata editing and links; section Options and page Options retain all existing commands.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
b.benefit: Emphasizes time while preserving ordering and spatial memory.
b.risk: Strong estimate hierarchy may overshadow deadlines.
b.verification: Verify overdue captions remain legible, unknown estimates are not zero and completion callbacks are unchanged.

a.title: Native details groups
a.mechanism: Use native Details groups with distinct scope-specific names; remeasure opened rows and preserve independent section collapse.
a.visible: Titles, exact period, active scope, completion and named summaries.
a.disclosed: Opened groups retain scope, duration, diagnostics and metadata editors; menus retain their current objects and callbacks.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
a.benefit: Uses predictable browser disclosure behavior with resilient text reflow.
a.risk: Virtualized list measurement must account for open details.
a.verification: Open nested groups at zoom, verify focus and heights, and test section collapse independently of metadata disclosure.

b.title: Sticky active-section context
b.mechanism: Keep a sticky active-section header with one sticky depth, bounded height and focus scroll margin; show exact global period and local scope, and retain local estimates, inclusion and Options without duplicating task metadata.
b.visible: Current section heading, small scope/count summary, selected period and completion. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
b.disclosed: Section summary opens estimates/inclusion; page summary and task details retain full data and actions. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
b.access: 44px sticky controls, bounded z-index, semantic headings and scroll margin for focused elements; no decorative blur on content. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
b.benefit: Keeps section operations reachable after scrolling without repeating metadata on tasks.
b.risk: Stacked nested sticky headings can cover content.
b.verification: Test nested section depths, focus scrolling, existing drag/drop menus, 320px height and historical context labels.
